 (BY SHRI MANISH DATT - SENIOR ADVOCATE WITH SHRI D.S.DUBEY -  ADVOCATE)

 This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e cour  following:
 ORDER
This second application for grant of bail in the form of criminal appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed assailing the order dated 01.09.2023 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Rewa (M.P.), whereby application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
for grant of regular bail filed on behalf of appellant/accused has been dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts: 2. Appellant has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. bearing Crime No.564/2022 dated 20.10.2022 registered at Police Station-Mangawa, District- Rewa (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 376, 306 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In the postmortem report death of deceased has been found due to hanging.
It is not a case of murder.
Present appellant in collusion with the police has deliberately concealed.
It is contended that appellant has criminal background of three cases.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
7. In this case, after investigation charge sheet has already been filed.
Mithailal Saket has already been examined before the trial Court.
As per postmortem report, death of the deceased was due to asphyxia.
DNA report does not confirm sexual act.
Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including the material on record, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant is not warranted.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Consequently, this appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 stands allowed and the impugned order dated 01.09.2023 passed by learned 12th Addl. Sessions Judge and Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Rewa is set- aside.
8. It is directed that appellant - Guru Prasad Tiwari be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
